title: GPU surge spillover postmortem - datapull manifest
summary: Data pull manifest and immediate analysis notes for the 2026-12-05 GPU surge + spillover event that caused elevated queue depths and cross-region throttle propagation. This sheet lists the raw tables/streams we pulled, the queries used, and initial anomalies to investigate for the postmortem writeup.
objective: Collect time-aligned telemetry from orchestration, serving runtime, and routing layers to determine root cause(s) of sudden capacity imbalance, why autoscaler did not replenish fast enough in eu-west1, and which throttle/routing policies propagated to other regions.
datasets_pulled: throttle_events: policy_id, reason, target_backend, start_ts, end_ts, affected_tenants
autoscaler_actions: decision_ts, group_id, delta_replicas, reason, cooldown_until
network_egress: cross-region egress bytes/s, NVLink/PCIe error counters
queries_run: peak_gpu_spike.sql -- align gpu_util_timeseries with requests to identify correlation windows
regional_queue_backfill.sql -- compute per-region queue depth and oldest_request_age 1m-averages
throttle_cascade_trace.sql -- join throttle_events to routing logs to find downstream propagation
autoscaler-timeline.sql -- reconstruct autoscaler decisions and cooldowns across the incident
fallback-frequency.sql -- count requests that hit fallback_variant grouped by tenant and minute
kvcache-eviction-spike.sql -- detect mass eviction events correlated with memory pressure
sample_sql_snippets:
-- sample, run with exported dataset names
SELECT ts, gpu_id, util_pct, mem_used_mb
FROM gpu_util_timeseries
WHERE ts >= '2026-12-05T02:00:00Z' AND ts <= '2026-12-05T06:00:00Z' AND region = 'eu-west1'
ORDER BY ts, gpu_id;

-- queue join
SELECT q.ts, q.region, q.queued_count, a.delta_replicas, t.policy_id
FROM request_queue_depth q
LEFT JOIN autoscaler_actions a ON floor(q.ts, '1m') = floor(a.decision_ts, '1m') AND q.group_id = a.group_id
LEFT JOIN throttle_events t ON q.region = t.target_region AND q.ts BETWEEN t.start_ts AND t.end_ts
ORDER BY q.ts;
initial_findings: 1) eu-west1 GPU median utilization jumped from 42% to 96% within a 6-minute window; several hosts hit sustained 99% and memory pressure triggered eviction events. 2) Autoscaler had a staggered cooldown policy (aggressive_down = 180s, conservative_up = 300s) which blocked immediate upscales for the cpus/gpu-mixed groups serving lower-priority traffic. 3) Throttle policy BETA-THROTTLE-3 was incorrectly applied to two dedicated pools, causing cross-region fallback traffic to route to smaller CPU-backed variants in us-central, increasing their latency and then feeding back as elevated queue depth. 4) KV cache hit rate dropped ~18% at 02:18 which amplified per-request compute due to missed reuse. 5) NVLink error counters increased slightly but not enough alone to explain the drop — likely cofactor with memory eviction.
